source.title: MAEBE: Multi-Agent Emergent Behavior Framework
source.venue: arXiv preprint (submitted to the Multi-Agent Systems Workshop, ICML 2025)

confidence_rationale: Mapping fidelity is the dominant term for an architectural test-scope claim, and here it is unusually high: the paper's headline result -- that ensemble moral reasoning is not predictable from isolated agent behaviour -- is close to a restatement of ARC-034's core assertion, arrived at independently. Confidence is held below 0.75 by source quality: this is an unrefereed preprint by independent researchers, using one benchmark (Greatest Good) at small ensemble scale, with no reported replication.
failure_signatures: An ensemble of LLM agents each of which passes an isolated moral-preference evaluation can still converge, under peer influence, on a group moral position none of them held alone -- so a per-agent pass certificate does not compose into an ensemble pass certificate.
Peer pressure shifted ensemble convergence even when an explicit supervisor agent was present, so adding a supervisory overseer does not by itself restore the validity of single-agent evaluation.

Single-agent moral preferences on instrumental harm were unstable under mere reframing (double-inversion questioning), so the n=1 baseline that a pairwise probe compares against is itself not a fixed quantity.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Traditional AI safety evaluations on isolated LLMs are insufficient as multi-agent AI ensembles become prevalent; the moral reasoning of LLM ensembles is not directly predictable from isolated agent behaviour, because of emergent group dynamics including peer pressure that persists under supervision.
mapping.ree_translation: This is direct external support for ARC-034's central negative assertion -- that local, first-order (n=1) ethical probes are insufficient to characterise the ethical properties of a multi-agent REE deployment -- and specifically for ARC-034's test-type (2), multi-agent stress testing. The observed non-composition of per-agent alignment into ensemble alignment is the same failure mode ARC-034 predicts when only pairwise interactions are probed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The agents here are LLMs prompted with a moral benchmark, not REE agents with the affective/valence substrate ARC-034 presupposes; 'moral preference' is a stated answer on a questionnaire, not a behavioural disposition arising from a care mechanism (cf. INV-001, which holds that REE has no explicit ethics module). The paper therefore supports the epistemics of ARC-034 -- that n=1 does not predict n=k -- without evidencing that the same holds for ethical properties grounded the way REE grounds them. It also demonstrates only the non-composition direction; it does not test ARC-034's converse case (locally depleted agents behaving MORE ethically at n=k), which is the MECH-127 motivating scenario.
mapping.source_context: LLM ensembles (Greatest Good Benchmark) with a double-inversion questioning technique; supervised and unsupervised ensemble conditions; text-based moral judgement outputs.

confidence_components.notes: Weighted toward mapping_fidelity per the architectural-claim rule. transfer_risk is moderate rather than high because both source and target are artificial multi-agent ensembles, so the structural transfer is short; the residual risk is entirely in the ethics construct, not in the multi-agent construct.
